observations: Source-lock160 adds a native-source SIP audience fence for the actual registered SIP controller/principal. Original and current scene groups, source lifecycle and exact target credential revision are checked at physical IO; no synthetic DtmfNativeRecipient is created and the already-owned source controller is not reentered. Pending releases all synchronous guards.

Five new controlled Core tests cover target credential ownership, Pending cleanup, rebound/retired target, actual registered principal/controller and private return. Ten current Core DTMF methods pass. These callback/scene tests are not SIP socket evidence.

The runtime registers the actual initial-SIP leg after connected Store admission. One original signed native batch freezes native and SIP recipients before IO and retains only original registrations/origins in queued work. Each gateway schedule has one stable ID, fresh independent named signal reads and exact actual source/call/Endpoint/Device/route custody.

Engine metadata is prepared before Store readers. The writer reserves its stable schedule before possible IO, uses the original sealed native source and actual route once, retains bounded named-signal readers only around actual writer work, then waits for physical leases to stop before recording local submission/not-started/uncertainty. Metadata contention and captured-outcome retries do not replay effects.

Three production methods run both EdDSA and ES256: actual INFO, actual negotiated RFC4733 and missing named receive permission. They retain one original SIP call, unchanged marked duplex thresholds and exact cleanup. INFO checks actual dialog/Contact Request-URI, digits/duration and a preexisting reserved journal row at real UDP receive. RFC4733 checks payload101, exact 800-sample terminal duration, events5/8/11 and at least three redundant end packets per event. Replay emits no additional tones.

Four actual SDK completed summaries validate against NativeDtmfSubmission in the existing HTTP/OpenAPI contract, with unique actual source observation IDs and gateway schedule IDs. The public SDK verifies signatures; the recorded DTO validator does not independently reverify signatures.

The initial call lifetime monitor now checks independent named signal directions if media authorization is withdrawn; each probe drops its read before the next probe. It constructs no RTP grant. This lifetime change is compiled but physical signal-only withdrawal is not yet qualified.

failed_or_retried_checks.observation: Five new tests initially failed because each test reconstructed a principal with a different expiry from the registered controller credential. Fixtures now use the actual credential snapshot; strict production validation was preserved. The corrected five and current ten-method suite pass.

The running build resolved the manifest before the new direct RTP parser dev dependency was added. It failed on missing rvoip_rtp_core. The locked manifest/lock graph was corrected and the current test build passes.

Cause remains unproven; the first failure remains an unresolved reliability observation.
